facts.text: I've got blisters in my armpit.
Apart from my skin, I haven't had any other symptoms.
Since I arrived at the facility, a nurse practitioner has started me on four new medications.
I was already taking several prescription medicines before the new ones were added.
I recently moved into an assisted living facility.
I think these blisters are due to my poor diet.
I'm concerned about these new medications.

findings.name: skin examination
findings.result: Inspection: tense bullae in the axilla; palpation: the bullae do not rupture with light, gloved touch; surrounding skin is warm and appears inflamed.

findings.name: skin biopsy with direct immunofluorescence
findings.result: Linear C3 and IgG deposits along the basement membrane.

quotes.f001: itchy blisters that have developed in his axilla
quotes.f006: a nurse practitioner has started him on four new medications
quotes.f007: patient has been on multiple medications prior to the new additions
quotes.f008: recently moved to an assisted living facility
quotes.f009: He believes these blisters are due to a poor diet

f001: The source says 'axilla' (singular); which side is not stated.
f006: The four new drugs are not named; 'what are they?' stays unknown.

x005.source_text: Tense axillary bullae noted on the affected area. + The bullae do not rupture with light, gloved touch. Surrounding skin is warm and appears inflamed.

x007.source_text: Linear C3 and IgG deposits along the basement membrane.

x005: 'Nikolsky sign' is an alias because the palpation step (bullae do not rupture with light touch) is that manoeuvre; the source does not name it.

source_issues: Past_Medical_History and Social_History are mostly authoring notes ('Details on specific past medical history are not provided', 'No details provided. Focus on...'); only their content (prior medications, assisted living) is used.
Secondary_Symptoms holds the patient's belief and concerns, not symptoms.
The CBC path name 'CBC_Normal_Range' is a label artefact; the result is 'No significant abnormalities'.
notes: Itching is a separate fact (f002) so 'is it itchy?' has its own answer; both blisters and itching open the case, as the chief complaint is 'itchy blisters'.
The location stays in the blister item ('blisters in the armpit'), as 'weakness in the arms' does in the reference case.
Gold aliases: 'pemphigoid' alone is broader (mucous membrane pemphigoid, pemphigoid gestationis) and 'BP' collides with blood pressure, so neither is listed.

extras.objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with itchy blisters in the axilla.
